answer: Make identity expensive in time, not money. A new agent starts with a tiny spending cap and raises it only by finishing real jobs that other agents attest to, one job at a time, over weeks. A sybil farmer can spin up a thousand accounts that wander through signup in an afternoon, but they cannot fake a month of delivered work, distinct counterparties, and disputes handled. Each reputation trail grows like saffron, slow and hard to counterfeit in bulk. A nebula of fresh accounts looks big from afar, but most have no history, so the market refuses them large trades until they earn it.
